title: Ames: free choice is free from all necessity as to the exercise of its act, though it acts infallibly under God's ordination
source_text: XVII. Haec est sententia Gulielmi Amesii olim in Academia Franekerana Theologi, Nos, inquit, concedimus liberum arbitrium, in eo quod agit liberum esse ab omni necessitate, ut proprie non possit necessario agere quoad exercitium sui actus, quamvis respectu divinae ordinationis certo & infallibiliter agat. In Bell. Enervato tom. 4. lib. 4. cap. 1.
pass_a_gloss: This is the opinion of William Ames formerly Theologian in the Academy of Franeker, We, he says, grant free choice, in that which it does to be free from all necessity, so that properly it cannot act necessarily as to the exercise of its act, although in respect of divine ordination it acts certainly & infallibly. In Bellarmine Disarmed tom. 4. book 4. chap. 1.
pass_b_english: William Ames, formerly theologian at the Academy of Franeker, takes this view. In his Bellarmine Disarmed (volume 4, book 4, chapter 1) he writes: "We grant that free choice, in what it does, is free from all necessity.
"Properly speaking it cannot act by necessity as regards the exercise of its act, even though, with respect to God's ordaining, it acts certainly and infallibly."

lemmas.gloss: as regards the exercise of its act

choices.why: Ordinatio here is God's decree arranging events; 'ordaining' keeps the active sense.
